evidence_artifact_basis: All files in Verification/ontology-first-release are scoped implementation/acceptance records for TASK-001 and TASK-031 through TASK-039. Disposable staging and native/initializer fixtures are excluded from source publication.
layout_adjustment_reason: Tests share three focused query suites; policy is integrated in the profile/state/publication contracts; durable operations use explicit intents and receipts directories. The original technical requirements and acceptance behavior are unchanged.
method: Reviewed each criterion against implementation, current deterministic tests and separately identified actual operation/native receipts. This report is evidence, not a mutation of managed plan or Task state.
native_task_scope: The completed native Task belongs only to the disposable representative project; the real root ledger and selected managed plan remain unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.text: Ontology operations identify their own canonical store and change boundary; creating, retrieving, or publishing ontology content does not create or activate a Task, alter role ownership, or merge canonical stores.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Canonical ontology, configuration, projections and durable control records have declared independent ownership. Real reads, publication and linking preserve root memory, governance and Task state.
requirements.title: Keep ontology project-local

acceptance_criteria.text: Operations reject unresolved, mismatched, or unspecialized project identity; path resolution prevents traversal or symlink escape into sibling projects or unselected filesystem locations.
Two projects with the same labels retain separate identities and lookup results.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Explicit root, saved identity and namespace are checked before selected-file loading. Neutral/mismatched identities, unsafe aliases and sibling references are rejected; separate initialized projects retain separate identities.
requirements.title: Resolve one explicit project identity and root

acceptance_criteria.text: A root query does not open a child project's ontology solely because it is under Projects/ or registered; child ontology changes do not silently change root results.
Registry-derived representations identify their registry source and do not authorize writes to the represented project.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Exact allowlists describe factual registry metadata without traversing child ontologies. Independent project inventories are preserved and later fixture source changes do not propagate into products.
requirements.title: Preserve child-project independence

acceptance_criteria.text: The supported JSON-LD profile and local context define record keys and their meanings; ordinary canonical parsing uses Python 3.12 standard-library JSON support.
Wiki pages, graph files, indexes, exports, and external tools are not alternative editable sources of canonical ontology facts.
ontology.yaml follows the project's documented JSON subset of YAML without introducing a core parser dependency.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: A strict compact JSON-LD graph profile and JSON-subset configuration use standard-library parsing. Canonical sources and generated products have separate declared paths.
requirements.title: Use one canonical authoring representation

acceptance_criteria.text: A record containing an HTTP context, an untrusted context, or an escaping file reference is rejected without network access or reading the target.
Core parsing does not advertise support for unrestricted JSON-LD processing; unsupported profile features receive an explicit diagnostic.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Only the pinned vendored context is accepted. Remote, nested, unknown and escaping references fail before target content is read; no general JSON-LD or RDF processing is advertised.
requirements.title: Keep JSON-LD context resolution local

acceptance_criteria.text: Two builds from identical ontology, configuration, referenced input bytes, module versions, and generator version produce byte-equivalent generated output.
Removing a generated projection loses no canonical knowledge; an explicit rebuild restores it and reports its input versions and digests.
compile and build-wiki modify only their declared generated destinations; failed input validation does not publish an apparently successful build or overwrite unrelated files.
Approval records, publication receipts, and accepted recovery state are durable records and are not classified or deleted as rebuildable projections.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Repeated root compile and wiki builds are byte-identical and retain canonical bytes. Deleted generated data rebuilds; unknown or edited destinations are preserved. Transaction tests distinguish durable intent/receipt recovery from generated output.
requirements.title: Make generated knowledge reproducible

acceptance_criteria.text: The core covers Project, ProjectTemplate, Artifact, Source, Specification, Requirement, Task, TRD, ImplementationPlan, Verification, Evidence, Agent, Role, Skill, Capability, ActionType, MemoryRecord, Lesson, Decision, OntologyConcept, Authority, and Scope, plus terms needed by the competency questions.
Concepts model meaning, capability, and relationships; a filesystem location is represented as an artifact binding rather than substituted for the concept.
Product-domain vocabulary and root-specific instances are absent from the reusable core.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Core 1.0.0 provides 65 portable concept/predicate/relation records, including the required vocabulary. The same core is locked in source, neutral starter, root and Template; project instances remain outside it.
requirements.title: Provide a reusable Sys4AI core module

acceptance_criteria.text: Missing modules or a digest/version mismatch produce a precise diagnostic and cannot be treated as a valid current import.
A newer depot module does not silently replace a project's selected imported version.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Version, complete content-map digest and manifest hash identify each import. Missing, extra or altered bytes and wrong versions fail; receipt-owned explicit refresh is separate from ordinary reruns.
requirements.title: Lock imported modules

acceptance_criteria.text: A project-local subtype or distinct concept can extend the selected core; an attempted incompatible redefinition of a core ID is rejected.
Project extensions remain local and do not automatically modify sys4ai-core or another project's ontology.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Local subtypes and distinct project IDs extend the core. Core redefinitions, duplicate and foreign namespace identities fail, and local extensions do not alter imported or sibling data.
requirements.title: Allow project extensions without redefining core identities

acceptance_criteria.text: Moving a bound artifact or changing a display label preserves the entity ID and existing references.
Imported core identities remain stable across projects; project-specific identities are unambiguous across project namespaces.
An identifier is not recycled for a different meaning.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Stable absolute semantic IDs remain independent of label and binding path. Local subtype/label movement retains identity; lifecycle validation rejects deletion and type/meaning recycling.
requirements.title: Keep semantic identities stable

acceptance_criteria.text: An approved concept with missing required metadata is invalid; a concept with supported optional explanatory fields retains them through reading and wiki generation.
Aliases resolve to the underlying stable identity rather than creating accidental duplicate concepts.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Approved/deprecated records require explanatory metadata and exact provenance. Aliases target the stable record; optional scope/examples and semantic relationships survive retrieval and wiki rendering.
requirements.title: Make concepts understandable and searchable

acceptance_criteria.text: term Task and term TRD return distinct definitions, stable IDs, relevant distinctions, and current source references.
Agent-facing answers do not equate document approval with Task activation or implementation completion, or verification with validation.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Task, TRD, ImplementationPlan, NativeGoal and conversation meanings are distinct. Root competency checks and actual Task/TRD output preserve approval/activation/completion and verification/validation boundaries.
requirements.title: Represent overloaded terminology explicitly

acceptance_criteria.text: The type Skill is distinguishable from the installed memory skill instance and the SKILL.md artifact that describes it; type and instance queries preserve that distinction.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Record kind distinguishes concept types from concrete skills and artifact bindings. Actual memory capability output identifies both the shared capability and installed provider; skill artifact identities remain separate.
requirements.title: Separate types from concrete instances

acceptance_criteria.text: A relationship has a registered predicate and typed endpoints; incoming and outgoing directions remain distinguishable.
Configured cardinality and qualifiers survive read/build operations, and invalid endpoint types or cardinalities fail validation.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Registered predicates declare domain, range, direction, cardinality and qualifiers. The deterministic validator rejects dangling or incorrectly typed endpoints and invalid configured cardinality/qualifiers.
requirements.title: Provide typed directional relationships

acceptance_criteria.text: Retrieval, graph projections, and wiki output identify the kind and source of each included fact.
Representing an inferred-fact category does not enable an inference engine or allow derived memory links to redefine canonical concepts.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Fact kind and exact provenance are retained in results, graph and generated pages. Derived memory associations remain versioned sidecars; classifying inferred facts does not run an inference engine.
requirements.title: Distinguish assertions from derived knowledge

acceptance_criteria.text: Bindings may point to selected SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, ROLE.md, SPECS.md, .agents/skills/, Roles/, and depot/projects.json content within the established project policy.
Unselected child content, credentials, secrets, private runtime data, environments, and caches are excluded; tests show that traversal and symlink references cannot bypass the binding policy.
Ontology binding setup leaves memory corpus configuration and exclusion rules unchanged.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: The root binds only exact selected governance, skill, role-pair and registry sources. Traversal, child roots, private state, credentials and aliases are rejected; memory exclusions/configuration are byte-preserved.
requirements.title: Use explicit source bindings

acceptance_criteria.text: A reviewer can resolve a returned definition to its recorded local source version and locator.
Changed, missing, or inaccessible source bytes are reported as stale or unavailable and cannot be presented as freshly verified current authority.
Validation and build results expose source/configuration/module/helper versions and hashes sufficient to reproduce their reported result.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Results expose source paths, hashes and typed locators plus complete configuration/module/helper context. Changed/missing source bytes are explicitly stale/unavailable, while current-authority reads expose the newly read source and discrepancy.
requirements.title: Trace definitions to exact source versions

acceptance_criteria.text: Resolving a capability, reading an action type, or validating an ontology does not invoke a skill or grant Task, role, tool, write, publication, or execution authority.
When a retrieved definition conflicts with current governing sources, the response identifies the discrepancy and uses those sources for operational rules.
ActionType may be described as vocabulary; installing execution interception or semantic pre-execution gates is excluded from this release.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Retrieval describes meaning and capability without invoking skills or assigning authority. Current-source discrepancies are surfaced. Exact ontology grants and existing Task writer gates govern separate mutations; no execution interception is installed.
requirements.title: Keep meaning separate from permission

acceptance_criteria.text: The writer supplies the exact reviewed change, reason, expected current digest, and applicable authority; stale content, missing authority, an ordinary child actor, or conflicting manager ownership prevents publication.
An authorized operation records what actually committed, preserves unrelated bytes, and exposes an exact receipt and bounded recovery result if publication is partial.
Ontology uses its own publication path and authority scope; possession of a memory publication grant alone does not authorize ontology writes.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Publication binds reviewed payload/reason/current digest and exact current Director or manager scope. Child, stale, memory-only and conflicting-owner grants fail. Accepted transactions and bounded partial recovery preserve unrelated bytes.
requirements.title: Require scoped approval for canonical ontology changes

acceptance_criteria.text: A deprecated ID remains resolvable with its deprecation reason and replacement when present; old references retain their historical meaning.
A changed definition cannot claim approval of the old bytes, and replacing a concept does not recycle its ID or silently rewrite history.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Deprecated IDs retain historical meanings and replacement metadata. Approved semantic edits need renewed review/history; deletion, identity recycling and unchanged approval of revised meaning fail.
requirements.title: Preserve lifecycle and deprecated references

acceptance_criteria.text: A suggestion or captured memory remains a proposal and cannot appear as an approved canonical definition without the required publication operation.
Rejected proposals and ambiguous extracted links do not silently change approved lookup results.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Suggestion transitions create provisional candidates, leaving inputs unchanged. Draft or ambiguous memory associations cannot rewrite an approved canonical definition.
requirements.title: Keep agent suggestions provisional

acceptance_criteria.text: Negative examples with a duplicate ID or unresolved relationship target fail with the offending ID and record location; equivalent valid examples pass.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Duplicate IDs and unresolved typed endpoints fail with stable actionable record diagnostics; valid equivalents pass the same deterministic check.
requirements.title: Validate identities and references

acceptance_criteria.text: An unmodeled collision fails validation; an explicitly modeled collision returns the candidate IDs and their distinctions rather than claiming an exact unambiguous resolution.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Unmodeled label/alias collisions fail; explicitly mutual ambiguity declarations require distinctions and return distinct candidate IDs instead of a guessed exact match.
requirements.title: Validate vocabulary ambiguity

acceptance_criteria.text: Focused invalid examples for each configured constraint fail with actionable diagnostics; strict-specialization cycles fail while a cycle in a relation not declared acyclic is not rejected solely for being a cycle.
Validation is deterministic and runs locally without an LLM, graph service, or optional standards backend.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Required metadata, typed relations, cardinalities, qualifiers and declared acyclic predicates have executable negative cases. Non-acyclic cycles remain valid; reordered records produce stable diagnostics without a service.
requirements.title: Validate semantic constraints deterministically

acceptance_criteria.text: Running each read operation preserves canonical files, generated files, configuration, and persistent timestamps, including when generated state is missing or stale.
Ordinary reads do not create directories, rebuild indexes on disk, install dependencies, start services, create Tasks, or publish proposals.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Every installed read scenario preserved 490 observed paths including bytes, mtimes and ctimes. Missing/stale generated-state tests prove reads create no directory or repair; no read creates Tasks or publishes.
requirements.title: Provide non-mutating ontology operations

acceptance_criteria.text: Stable-ID and exact-label lookup precede alias and general lexical matches; approved exact matches are not displaced by looser matches.
An unknown term reports no match; an ambiguous term returns explicit alternatives with IDs and distinctions.
Retrieval works without embeddings or an external semantic service.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Stable IDs and exact labels precede aliases and lexical matches with deterministic tie breaks. Unknown/ambiguous vocabulary is explicit, and lexical/core lookup succeeds with site packages disabled.
requirements.title: Resolve identifiers and vocabulary deterministically

acceptance_criteria.text: neighbors Task returns typed relationships from the selected graph; path Task MemoryRecord returns a meaningful path within limits or explicitly reports none.
A cyclic or densely connected example terminates within the configured limits and identifies any truncation; relation direction and allowed predicates are preserved.
No fixed performance target or arbitrary hop count is implied; supported limits and defaults are documented.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Typed incoming/outgoing traversal and predicate filters retain direction. Cycles terminate with declared hop/result/serialized-byte limits and explicit truncation; actual Task neighbors and Task-to-MemoryRecord path are recorded.
requirements.title: Bound graph-based context expansion

acceptance_criteria.text: A human or agent can distinguish ID, preferred-label, alias, lexical, or graph-traversal matches and identify their source versions.
Draft and deprecated results are explicitly labeled and cannot be mistaken for currently approved definitions.
Machine-readable output and concise human-facing rendering convey the same result identity and evidence.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Machine and human results identify the same stable identity, source evidence and match reason. Lifecycle and source freshness remain explicit; deprecated replacement and lexical truncation are observed.
requirements.title: Return explainable ontology results

acceptance_criteria.text: Missing configuration, invalid modules, missing projections, stale source hashes, and an empty project extension produce specific diagnostics.
Valid empty project extensions can use the imported core; stale generated data is not presented as a verified current answer.
Any suggested compile or repair remains a separate explicit operation.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Health distinguishes missing identity/config, import errors, empty usable extensions, source freshness and missing/stale projections. Reads retain valid canonical results and leave repairs explicit.
requirements.title: Report readiness without hidden repair

acceptance_criteria.text: A generated Task page explains its distinction from TRD and links to related concepts and recorded governing sources.
Pages identify themselves as generated, preserve source/classification information, and direct canonical edits to their owning records.
A wiki rebuild never imports hand-edited page content as canonical ontology.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Generated Task pages state their TRD distinction, owning canonical location, fact classification and source versions. Edited generated content is never parsed as canonical knowledge.
requirements.title: Generate readable concept pages

acceptance_criteria.text: A reader can start at the wiki index, find Task or a memory capability, follow a relationship, and reach its source reference.
Repeated builds have stable filenames and links; validation detects broken generated internal links.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: The actual index-to-Task and memory-capability walkthrough follows relationships and local sources. Stable filenames and repeated bytes were verified; a deliberately broken link is detected in tests.
requirements.title: Make the wiki navigable

acceptance_criteria.text: Capability-to-skill and skill-to-capability queries resolve project memory retrieval and TRD creation to their installed skill sources.
The to-trd binding accurately states that creating a TRD does not create a Task.
Missing or changed skill sources are reported as unavailable or stale; capability discovery invokes no skill.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Actual capability/skill queries identify installed memory and to-trd sources and execution limits. Core competency checks enforce the TRD-not-Task distinction; changed provider sources are stale and discovery invokes nothing.
requirements.title: Bind skills to capabilities

acceptance_criteria.text: Queries identify the artifacts defining a role using its actual AGENTS.md and ROLE.md pair, rather than treating Roles/INDEX.md as authority.
The graph distinguishes the host Director from a confirmed Task manager and an ordinary child; ontology lookup neither assigns a role nor changes canonical role or Task state.
Bindings represent selected relevant metadata without requiring a rewrite of every role, skill, or specification file.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Role bindings contain their exact same-directory AGENTS.md/ROLE.md pairs. Queries distinguish host Director, confirmed Task manager and ordinary child without editing those roles or the Task ledger.
requirements.title: Bind roles and governance artifacts to their meanings

acceptance_criteria.text: Definition and vocabulary queries use ontology and its source references; relationships use the bounded graph; historical questions use memory.

Current-authority queries read the current governing sources first; mixed queries resolve ontology terminology, retrieve memory evidence, and verify current sources when an answer concerns current behavior.
A capability request returns its skill and constraints without executing the operation.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Definition, relationship, capability, current, history and mixed routes use the intended ontology, graph, current-source and installed-memory interfaces. Actual current-governance and historical outputs retain their source categories.
requirements.title: Route knowledge queries by intent

acceptance_criteria.text: Ontology publication and linking leave existing memory records byte-identical and valid under the current schema; no ontology_refs field is inserted.
Memory publication or automatic capture leaves canonical ontology unchanged.
Ontology setup does not broaden the memory corpus, activate a new memory backend, migrate memory, or alter its existing capture setting.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Actual reciprocal publication proves ontology writes/linking preserve schema-1 memory, while real memory supersession preserves ontology. Root memory corpus, records, backend and capture setting remain unchanged.
requirements.title: Preserve canonical memory and its retrieval policy

acceptance_criteria.text: Explicit link generation creates associations only for the selected project's accessible records and resolvable concepts; memory records remain unchanged.
Ambiguous or unmatched associations are identified rather than published as canonical facts.
After a source record or ontology version changes, stale associations are detected; explicit rebuilding reproduces current links and does not reuse stale links as verified evidence.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Explicit sidecars link accessible record versions to resolvable concepts; ambiguity/unmatched results are recorded. A real supersession makes links stale, excludes them from current evidence, and explicit rebuild restores current links without canonical writes.
requirements.title: Build derived memory-to-concept links

acceptance_criteria.text: A query about prior Task manager failures resolves TaskManager-related terminology and retrieves relevant existing historical memory through the supported memory interface.
Expansion cannot bring excluded sources, another project's records, stale evidence, or new live records into a frozen solver context.
The response identifies no matching historical evidence or unavailable memory when applicable, without inventing records or provisioning a backend.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Ontology terms expand queries through supported memory reads and preserve memory exclusions. Actual prior-manager query returns real historical evidence; unavailable/no-match and frozen-new-record cases do not invent evidence or provision a backend.
requirements.title: Use ontology to improve memory query selection

acceptance_criteria.text: A mixed response identifies each source type, exact concept or record identity, source version, and relevant evidence.
Historical memory is not upgraded to operational authority by a concept link, and an ontology match is not presented as proof that a historical event occurred.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Mixed results label ontology definitions, memory record identities/versions and current governing sources separately. Concept matches and historical associations never become event proof or operational permission.
requirements.title: Keep mixed knowledge evidence distinguishable

acceptance_criteria.text: The current confirmed manager can freeze an explicit selected or empty packet within its granted output scope and register it through existing Task artifact/input mechanisms.
The complete packet digest is held in its external artifact reference; the packet does not need a self-referential hash.
Packets obey the current Task reference and artifact limits, exclude sibling drafts and prohibited sources, and introduce no Task schema field or activation route.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: A confirmed native manager freezes/registers exact packets through current Task artifacts, baseline and assignment APIs. External artifact digests avoid self-hashes; empty/oversize/owner/scope and sibling inputs are tested without a Task schema change.
requirements.title: Freeze ontology context as existing Task inputs

acceptance_criteria.text: Each initial assignment references identical ontology packet bytes and permitted source versions.
Publishing new ontology content after dispatch leaves the packet unchanged; a changed referenced file is detected and not silently substituted.
Further ontology retrieval for that round is limited to its frozen content and explicitly permitted exact sources.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Two actual independent solver contexts received identical 13-record packet/source inputs. A later publication remained excluded in both; changing a selected source rejected the old packet, and current retrieval stayed within the frozen selection.
requirements.title: Keep independent solver inputs identical

acceptance_criteria.text: Ontology operations create, resume, complete, or upgrade no Task and do not alter its required team or writer.
A change affecting current solver meaning is assessed by the confirmed manager and reaches affected workers only through the existing versioned input, reconciliation, review, and acceptance gates.
An immaterial change retains its reason without requiring an automatic restart.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Ontology routines never create or complete Tasks. The real confirmed manager used existing reserve/input/reconcile/version/senior/acceptance gates for same-ID material reassessment and documented immaterial late-content isolation.
requirements.title: Use existing Task ownership and reassessment

acceptance_criteria.text: Authoritative additions originate in ONTOLOGY-depo/, SKILLS-depo/ontology/, and the affected existing reusable source collections; the Template receives them through tools/template_update.py.
The update check reports the exact mapped additions and any conflicts before application; affected source/Template contracts validate after application.
Only the registered Template is automatically updated; unrelated project-local installations remain unchanged.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Seventy-five reviewed source files were promoted under the existing updater lock; the real updater applied 57 additions and 16 updates with zero deletes. Final Template mapping is current, and independent projects remain unchanged.
requirements.title: Distribute reusable ontology through the existing Template pipeline

acceptance_criteria.text: The installed root commands resolve project sys4ai-depot and answer the initial competency questions using current root sources.
Root adoption records the selected source versions and exact changed artifacts, and preserves existing memory, learning, Task, role, licensing, and independent project state.
The operation does not restore an old ontology or Memory Service runtime or inherit authority from historical records.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Root adoption records exact source/root hashes and published seed scope. Installed commands resolve sys4ai-depot with 28 passing competency questions; memory, learning, Task, role, licenses, old runtime absence and independent projects are preserved.
requirements.title: Adopt the first release in the Sys4AI depot root

acceptance_criteria.text: A Template content inventory contains the reusable capability and core module but no sys4ai-depot instance data, root actor binding, memory links, generated graph/index/cache/wiki build state, or project-private source references.
An empty project extension is distinguished from missing required capability.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: The actual Template has null project identity/namespace, disabled unbound publication, empty extension/bindings and locked portable core. It contains no root ontology instances, derived links, wiki or ontology runtime/control state.
requirements.title: Keep the Template neutral

acceptance_criteria.text: Disposable create and first-prepare runs produce distinct project identities/namespaces and exact destination-local authority references without root project data.
Setup receipts distinguish copied assets, specialized configuration, preserved content, and actual capability readiness.
Initialization installs no external ontology service, RDF backend, embedding model, or product runtime.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Actual create and first preparation specialize distinct IDs/namespaces and local Director bindings. Their receipts separate copied/configured/preserved/static-ready state from runtime and current grants; no service or package is provisioned.
requirements.title: Specialize ontology during new-project setup

acceptance_criteria.text: An ordinary rerun of an earlier completed setup neither adds ontology nor relabels the project's base setup edition.
A selected adoption records source/destination identity, exact module and file versions, overwrite boundaries, preserved content, and current readiness through the existing receipt/recovery model.
No real existing product project receives ontology solely because this release is installed in the depot or Template.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Actual v7 reruns install no ontology and retain the original edition. Selected adoption appends scoped module receipts; later unchanged-owned refresh is explicit. No real existing product is adopted.
requirements.title: Support explicit adoption by existing projects

acceptance_criteria.text: A destination containing a customized, incomplete, or incompatible ontology package is preserved and receives precise diagnostics rather than a partial merge or false ready claim.
Existing memory backend/capture settings, historical records, licenses, and bound governance remain unchanged unless the user separately selects the exact applicable change.
Interrupted adoption resumes only its same recorded request and expected bytes; changed inputs or conflicting edits prevent unsafe replay.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: A real customized incomplete package stays whole with precise unavailable diagnostics. Governance/licensing/memory/capture settings survive; deterministic interruption/tamper tests enforce exact same-request recovery and reject drift.
requirements.title: Preserve project-owned content during adoption

acceptance_criteria.text: The ontology core acceptance checks pass with no graph database, RDFLib, pySHACL, LLM, vector index, or network service available.
Ontology lookup remains usable when the optional memory backend is unavailable; mixed queries report the memory limitation while retaining valid ontology results.
Ordinary reads and project setup do not install or initialize optional dependencies.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Installed core lookup and all structural/competency checks pass with Python site packages disabled. Optional-memory unavailable cases retain valid ontology results and report limitations; nothing installs dependencies or starts services.
requirements.title: Keep the first-release core service-independent

acceptance_criteria.text: A reader can resolve Task, inspect a capability, follow provenance, build the wiki explicitly, and identify the required authority for a proposed canonical edit using documented examples.
Documentation distinguishes semantic retrieval from execution, generated files from authoring files, setup from operational readiness, and document approval from implementation authority.
Unimplemented later features are labeled out of scope rather than advertised as available.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Installed/source documentation provides authoring, retrieval, graph, wiki, review/grant and integration examples. It distinguishes semantics, history, current authority and setup readiness and labels future RDF/inference/service features out of scope.
requirements.title: Document authoring, retrieval, and integration

acceptance_criteria.text: The initial checks cover Project and Task meaning; Task versus TRD; project memory and its authority limits; memory-retrieval capability; Task management; role source artifacts; verification versus validation; Template derivation; child-project authority; memory-publication relations; deprecated replacements; and definition provenance.
Each question has an observable expected concept, relationship, distinction, source, or explicit no-result outcome; success is not defined as an LLM declaring its own answer correct.
Project extensions can add competency questions without changing the shared core vocabulary.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Fourteen core and fourteen root competency questions assert concrete IDs, distinctions, sources, capabilities, relationships and no-result expectations. Project questions are separately selected without rewriting core vocabulary.
requirements.title: Specify executable competency questions

acceptance_criteria.text: The local automated run executes both groups, fails if either fails, and reports exact input versions and results.

Negative cases cover duplicate IDs, dangling targets, label ambiguity, missing approved metadata/provenance, invalid relation types/cardinality, acyclic-relation violations, unsafe source paths, and remote JSON-LD contexts.
CI invocation is documented and connected to any applicable existing pipeline; hosted CI provisioning or remote publication is not required to run these checks locally.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: The combined entry point reports structural and competency results plus complete context; either negative group fails the run. Profile/semantic/path adversarial cases and documented local CI commands are exercised.
requirements.title: Run structural and competency checks together

acceptance_criteria.text: An agent resolves Task and TRD with the intended distinctions, finds the memory capability for a relevant lexical query, traverses Task relationships, and receives a meaningful bounded path or explicit no-path result.
Deprecated lookup identifies its replacement where present; a current-governance query reads governing sources; a mixed prior-failure query returns real memory evidence or accurately reports none.
Recorded outputs identify the project, source versions, query route, and result evidence; a valid schema alone is not sufficient acceptance.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Fifteen actual installed CLI scenarios record project, source context, route and results for terminology, capability, traversal/path, deprecated replacement, current sources, history and no-match; this is separate from deterministic suite evidence.
requirements.title: Verify actual agent-facing retrieval

acceptance_criteria.text: Create and first preparation yield neutral but specialized ontology capability; an older completed receipt acquires ontology only through the selected adoption route.
Customized content, prior setup editions, memory preferences, licensing, and project-local data survive reruns and adoption.
Root queries remain isolated from the representative child projects, and reusable changes do not propagate into them automatically.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Actual create, first-prepare, prior-edition rerun/adoption, customization and refresh receipts demonstrate identity specialization and preservation. A fixture-only source change did not propagate to the initialized child; root lookup remained local.
requirements.title: Verify Template and initializer behavior

acceptance_criteria.text: Before/after digests show that ontology publication/linking preserves canonical memory and memory publication preserves canonical ontology.
A representative Task input/assignment flow registers and delivers the same packet digest to the independent solver contexts; a subsequent ontology change cannot enter those frozen contexts silently.
Read operations leave canonical and generated state unchanged; unauthorized publication is rejected even when ontology validation succeeds.
Evidence distinguishes deterministic tests from directly observed agent/Task integration and does not claim unexercised runtime behavior.

requirements.reviewed_conclusion: Actual reciprocal ontology/memory transactions, immutable native packets delivered to two independent contexts and same-ID reassessment have exact receipts. Byte/timestamp nonmutation and real ordinary-child rejection are recorded separately from synthetic unit scenarios.
requirements.title: Verify memory and Task integration boundaries

acceptance_criteria: The TRD revision/digest and live dependencies are identified; a changed requirement or conflicting owner stops dependent work for reassessment.
The manifest names each authorized source/root/Template destination and every protected path, including pre-existing records and independent projects.
Read-only updater status and any existing watcher behavior are recorded without new service installation.
tasks.title: Record current inputs and preservation inventory

acceptance_criteria: Each supported field, local context, stable identity, module lock, relation qualifier and fact classification has a documented meaning; unsupported JSON-LD features fail explicitly.
Canonical ONTOLOGY/modules and bindings plus ontology.yaml are separate from generated .sys4ai/ontology and ONTOLOGY/WIKI; control_records/ontology holds durable publication records.
The core contract requires only Python 3.12 standard-library capabilities and rejects remote context resolution.
tasks.title: Specify the supported ontology profile and state paths

acceptance_criteria: Every operation declares its input, output, write scope and authority; read commands perform no persistent repair and discovery never executes a skill.
Publication uses its own exact reviewed payload, current expected hashes and scoped authority; a memory grant is insufficient.
Packet construction, native assignment validation, frozen-source restrictions and material reassessment use existing Task interfaces and limits.
tasks.title: Specify publication, command and integration contracts

acceptance_criteria: Wrong/missing/neutral identities, duplicate JSON keys, traversal, symlinks, forbidden source paths, remote contexts and unsupported profile features fail with bounded diagnostics.
Loading opens only selected modules and bindings; same-label projects remain isolated and no network or package setup occurs.
tasks.title: Implement safe project and profile loading

acceptance_criteria: All 22 named REQ-007 concepts and terms needed by REQ-050 are modeled, including TaskManager, NativeGoal, CodexConversation and Validation distinctions.
